JUDGMENT

The brief
facts leading to the filing of the present petition are that the petitioner
filed a suit for recovery of maintenance allowance; she got an ex party decree
passed against the respondent No. 1 vide judgment and decree dated 2-9â€‘1986
by the Judge, Family Court, Lahore. The respondent No. 1 filed an. application for
setting aside the said judgment and decree on 16â€‘11â€‘1986 which was
resisted by the present petitioner. Can 28â€‘6â€‘1989 the evidence of
the respondent No.1 was recorded as the Court hours were over, the counsel for
the petitioner requested for adjournment of the case for next day for cross -examination.
His request was turned down. The petitioner filed an application for recall of
the witness which was also dismissed on 16â€‘9â€‘1989. The petitioner
challenged the order dated 28â€‘6â€‘1989 and 16â€‘9â€‘1989 in
W.P. No.776 of 1990 which was disposed of with the observation that the
petitioner could challenge the interim orders when the final order in the
instant suit is passed. Thereupon the petitioner produced evidence and the
learned Judge, Family Court vide judgment and decree dated 31â€‘1â€‘1993
accepted the application of the respondent No.1 and set aside the ex parte
decree passed on 2â€‘9â€‘1986. The petitioner has now challenged the
order dated 31â€‘1â€‘1993, 28â€‘6â€‘1989 and 16â€‘9â€‘1989
being passed without lawful authority. Without keeping in view the present law,
the learned Judge, Family Court should have given an opportunity of crossâ€‘examination
to the petitioner since she had produced a registered acknowledgement due of
the service of notice upon the respondent No.1 which was annexed with the reply
of the petitioner. Since the petitioner was not given an opportunity of crossâ€‘examination
so the learned Judge, Family Court could not adjudicate the matter judiciously.

2. I have
seen the acknowledgement due received by the respondent No.1. Under proviso to
subsection (2) of section 7 of the West Pakistan Family Courts Act, 1964 the
parties may with the permission of the Court call any witness at any later
stage if the Court considers such evidence expedient in the interest of justice.
So far as the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner is concerned
they seem very reasonable because the learned Judge, Family Court was to look
for setting aside an ex parte decree in favour of the petitioner and against
the respondent, he was under the duty to give opportunity of crossâ€‘examination
to the petitioner which has not been afforded to her although the provisions of
the Family Curt Act allow the evidence to be called at the later stage.

3. In view
of the above observation, I accept this petition, set aside the orders dated 28â€‘6â€‘1989,
16â€‘9â€‘1989 and 31â€‘1â€‘1993 passed by the learned Judge,
Family Court and remand this case back to the Judge, Family Court, Lahore so as
to provide an opportunity of crossâ€‘examination of the evidence of
respondent No.1 in the application for setting aside the ex parte decree and
after careful scrutiny of the same decide the case afresh.
